title: Therapy in English in Barcelona: Cost and How to Choose
description: What therapy in English costs in Barcelona in 2026, public vs private options, and how to check a psychologist's credentials before you book.
excerpt: Private therapy in Barcelona is more affordable than in many countries, but titles are not all regulated. Here is what to expect and what to check.
tldr: In 2026 a private therapy session in Barcelona typically costs roughly €50 to €100 for 45 to 60 minutes, with English-speaking therapists often at the higher end. Check that your therapist is a registered psychologist, because the titles psychotherapist and coach are not protected in Spain.

segments.text: Finding a therapist who works in your own language can make a real difference, and Barcelona has a sizeable community of English-speaking psychologists and counsellors. The main things to understand are how much sessions cost, how the public and private routes differ, and how to tell a properly qualified professional from someone who simply uses the word therapist.

content.text: How much does therapy in English cost in Barcelona in 2026?

segments.text: Private therapy in Barcelona typically costs about €50 to €100 per session in 2026, with sessions running 45 to 60 minutes. Sources give different ranges, from around €40 to €90 for general Spanish rates to €80 to €125 for specialist English-speaking practices in Madrid and Barcelona, so expect the figure to depend on the therapist's training and experience. English-speaking practitioners often charge more than Spanish-language ones because of demand and extra training.

items: Clinical or health psychologist: roughly €50 to €90 per session.
Psychiatrist (a medical doctor who can prescribe): roughly €60 to €120 per session.
Specialist English-language practices: often around €80 to €100 or more.
Couples or family sessions: usually higher, and often longer.

segments.text: Some therapists offer a lower rate to students or people on low incomes, and many offer online sessions at the same price. Ask about cancellation terms before your first appointment, as many practices charge for late cancellations.

content.text: Is therapy available on the public system?

segments.text: Yes, but access is slow and services are mainly in Spanish and Catalan. Public mental health care in Spain is free at the point of use and starts with a referral from your GP, and reports describe long waiting times and a limited number of sessions. Many expats therefore use a private psychologist, or use private insurance that covers a set number of sessions. Our guide to
seeing a doctor in English in Barcelona
explains how the public route works.

content.text: Does private health insurance cover therapy?

segments.text: Sometimes. Some private plans cover a yearly allowance of psychology sessions, often with a small copayment of roughly €10 to €15 per session, while couples therapy and coaching are usually excluded. Policies differ a lot, so check the number of sessions, whether you need a referral, and whether you must use a therapist in the insurer's network before you book.

content.text: What is the difference between a psychologist, psychiatrist and psychotherapist?

items: A psychologist has a university degree in psychology, and a health or clinical psychologist has further qualification to treat mental health conditions.
A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who can diagnose and prescribe medication.
A psychotherapist or counsellor may be a psychologist or come from another background, and the titles psychotherapist and coach are not legally protected in Spain.

content.text: How do I check a therapist's credentials in Spain?

segments.text: Ask for the therapist's registration number with the professional body, the Col·legi Oficial de Psicologia de Catalunya for psychologists working in Catalonia, and check it. A qualified therapist will be happy to share their training and registration. Also ask which approach they use, for example cognitive behavioural therapy, and whether they have experience with your concern, such as anxiety, relocation stress or relationship difficulties.

Both work, and many therapists offer either. In person can feel easier for building trust, while online widens your choice and suits busy schedules. If you choose online, confirm the therapist is registered in Spain or the country where they practise, and check how they handle privacy and data.

content.text: What if I need help urgently?

segments.text: If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 112, Spain's emergency number. Spain also has a free national suicide crisis line, 024, which answers around the clock. Therapy sessions are not an emergency service.

content.text: What happens in a first therapy session?

segments.text: The first session is usually an assessment. The therapist asks what brings you in, your history and what you hope to change, and explains how they work, how often you would meet and how confidentiality operates. It is also your chance to judge whether you feel comfortable with them. It is normal to try one or two therapists before settling, and a good therapist will not be offended if you do.

content.text: What questions should I ask before booking?

items: Are you a registered psychologist, and what is your registration number?
Do you work in English for the whole session, including any written notes or reports?
What is your fee, session length and cancellation policy?
Do you offer online sessions, and is there a difference in price?
How many sessions do you expect I might need, and how will we review progress?
Do you invoice in a way my insurer accepts?

segments.text: This guide is general information, not medical or psychological advice. Prices change, so check the current fee with the practice.

faqs.q: How much does therapy cost in Barcelona?
faqs.a: In 2026 a private session typically costs about €50 to €100 for 45 to 60 minutes. English-speaking specialists are often at the higher end.

faqs.q: Can I get therapy in English on the Spanish public system?
faqs.a: Public mental health care is free but usually starts with a GP referral, has long waits and is mainly in Spanish and Catalan, so many expats choose a private English-speaking therapist.

faqs.q: Is a psychotherapist the same as a psychologist in Spain?
faqs.a: No. Psychologist is a regulated title based on a degree, while psychotherapist and coach are not legally protected, so ask for qualifications and registration.

faqs.q: Does health insurance in Spain cover therapy?
faqs.a: Some private plans cover a yearly allowance of psychology sessions, often with a small copayment, but couples therapy and coaching are usually excluded.

faqs.q: Is online therapy in English available for Barcelona residents?
faqs.a: Yes. Many English-speaking therapists in Barcelona offer online sessions, usually at similar prices to in-person appointments.
